source_text: In illud: Pater si possibile est Τοῦ ὁσίου πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀμφιλοχίου ἐπισκόπου Ἰκονίου λόγος κατὰ αἱρετικῶν εἰς τό· Πάτερ εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρελθέτω ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο. Πάλιν ὡς στρατιώτης ἔννομος τὴν πρὸς τοὺς αἱρετικοὺς ἀναδέχομαι μάχην, ταξιαρχοῦντος Στεφάνου τοῦ στρατηγοῦ τῆς εὐσεβείας. Ὥσπερ γὰρ Μωϋσέως προσευχομένου Ἰησοῦς ἐτροποῦτο τοὺς πολεμίους, οὕτω κἀγὼ τοῦ μάρτυρος συνεργοῦντος τοὺς ἐχθροὺς χειροῦμαι τῆς ἀληθείας. Ταῦτα λέγω οὐ περιουσίᾳ λόγων θαρρῶν, ἀλλὰ τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ μάρτυρος πεποιθώς· διὸ καὶ θαρρῶν ἐφάπτομαι τῶν λόγων. Οὐ δειλιῶ γὰρ αὐτῶν τὸν ἐν λόγοις ὄγκον. Ἀφοβοῦμαι τῆς κακοτέχνου ἀπάτης τὰ προβλήμα τα. Ἔμαθον γὰρ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι φόβον οὗ οὐκ ἦν φόβος. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ Χριστὸν φοβεῖσθαι καὶ δειλιᾶν τὸν θάνατον λέγουσιν, ἡμεῖς δὲ διὰ Χριστὸν ὅσας ἐν σαρκὶ ζῶμεν ἡμέρας, τοσαυτάκις ἀποθανεῖν αἱρούμεθα, ἵνα γυμνῇ τῇ κεφαλῇ θριαμβεύσωμεν τὴν ἀλήθειαν. Ὅθεν ὡς ἤδη τὴν νικῶσαν ψῆφον ἔχων χωρῶ κατ' αὐτῶν. Χρισ τὸς γάρ με διὰ τοῦ προφήτου παραθαρρύνει λέγων· Υἱὲ ἀνθρώ που, μὴ φοβηθῇς ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτῶν, διότι παροιστρήσουσιν ἐπὶ σὲ κύκλῳ. Ἐν μέσῳ γὰρ σκορπίων σὺ κατοικεῖς. Σκορπίους γὰρ νύττοντας οὐ φοβοῦμαι. Οὐ γὰρ γυμνῷ ποδὶ βαδίζω· ἔχω γὰρ τὰ ὑποδήματα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης, ἵνα κἂν δηχθῶ μὴ βλαβῶ. Καὶ ὑποδησάμενοι, φησίν, τοὺς πόδας ἐν ἑτοιμασίᾳ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τῆς εἰρήνης. Φέρε οὖν τοῖς ὑποδήμασι τῆς εἰρήνης τὴν πολύμορφον τῶν αἱρετικῶν πατήσωμεν κεφαλήν, ἵνα δι' ὧν ἀφόβως κατ' αὐτῶν χωροῦμεν, διδάξωμεν αὐτοὺς ὡς μεγάλα σφάλλονται φόβον καὶ δειλίαν τῇ ἐπὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς προσάπτοντες φύσει. Οἱ γὰρ πάντα ἀκρίτως καὶ ἀλογίστως νοοῦντες καὶ λαλοῦντες καὶ τὸ Πάτερ εἰ δυνατὸν παρελθάτω τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο μὴ συνιέντες δειλίαν τοῦ Χριστοῦ καταψηφίζονται καὶ ἐνδεῆ αὐτὸν καὶ ἐλάττονα λέγουσιν τῷ πρὸς τὸν πατέρα προσεύχεσθαι καὶ ζητεῖν τῆς ἐπικειμένης ἀνάγκης τὴν λύτρωσιν. Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐφ' ὕβρει τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διαβάλλουσι λόγον καὶ ἐπ' ἀθετήσει τοῦ πνεύματος τὸ γράμμα περιᾴδουσιν κωμῳδοῦντες καὶ διασύροντες τὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ οἰκονομίαν, καὶ δεινότητι φράσεως καὶ εὐφραδίᾳ ῥη μάτων τὰ ἰοβόλα αὐτῶν ἐπικαλύπτουσι δήγματα, τῶν ἀκεραιο τέρων ἀποσυλῶντες τὴν σωτηρίαν, δεῦρο ὡς λόγων ἄπειροι αὐτὸν τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπικαλεσόμεθα λόγον, ἵνα αὐτὸς τῶν ἑαυτοῦ λόγων ἑρμηνεὺς γενόμενος ἐκείνων μὲν στηλιτεύσῃ τὴν ἄνοιαν, ἡμῶν δὲ στηρίξῃ τὴν διάνοιαν. Φράσον ἡμῖν τῶν εἰρημένων τὴν ἔννοιαν, δέσποτα, ἀνάπτυξον τὴν φυλλίδα τοῦ γράμματος καὶ δεῖξον τὸν καρπὸν τοῦ πνεύμα τος, ἵνα μὴ τῷ γράμματι προσέχοντες ἀποθάνωμεν, ἀλλ' ἵνα τῷ πνεύματι προσδραμόντες τῆς ζωῆς ἀπολαύσωμεν. Τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀποκτείνει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωοποιεῖ. Ἡμᾶς δίδαξον ὡς νήπιον, τοὺς δὲ αἱρετικοὺς παίδευσον ὡς ἄφρονας· παιδευτὴς γὰρ εἶ ἀφρόνων καὶ διδάσκαλος νηπίων. Ἡμῖν ὡς νηπίοις τὸν μαζὸν τῆς χάριτος γύμνωσον καὶ τὴν θηλὴν τοῦ πνεύματος ἐπιδούς. Τὸ καθαρὸν τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς διδασκαλίας ἐπιχεθῇ γάλα. Τῶν δὲ αἱρετικῶν τὴν ἀφροσύνην δήλην ποίησον. Εἰ μὴ γὰρ ἦσαν ἄφρονες, οὐκ ἂν ἐπ' ἀναιρέσει σου τῆς θεότητος βλασφημίας ὕφαναν δόγμα. Εἶπεν γὰρ ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἄφρων, φησίν, οὐκ ἔστι θεός. Γύμνωσον αὐτῶν τὸ πρόσχημα τῆς ἀσεβείας, ἵνα φανῇ τὸ δρᾶμα τῆς ὑποκρίσεως. ∆εῖξον ὡς διὰ τοῦτο τὴν σὴν προσηγορίαν περιφέρουσι, 1 ἵνα τῆς οἰκείας προαιρέσεως τὴν βλασφημίαν ἐπικαλύψωσιν. Εἰπὲ οὖν, δέσποτα, τίνος ἕνεκεν ἐπὶ τὸ πάθος ἐλθὼν παραιτῇ τὸ παθεῖν, διὰ τί δὲ φοβῇ τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπειλήν, ὁ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τοὺς ἀποκτέννοντας τὸ σῶμα παρεγγυώμενος. Ὅλως δὲ εἰ φοβῇ τὸν θάνατον, τί οὐ παραιτῇ τὸν θάνατον; Εἰ γὰρ ἐν σοὶ κεῖται τὸ παθεῖν καὶ τὸ μὴ παθεῖν, περιττῶς λέγεις τό· Εἰ δυνατὸν παρελ θάτω. Ἐν σοὶ γάρ
thought_title: Opening: the preacher arms himself for battle against heretics
orientation: Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, opens his homily against heretics by presenting himself as a soldier under the martyr Stephen's protection, then turns to Christ and asks him to interpret his own words in the Garden.
pass_a_gloss: Again as a lawful soldier I take up the battle against the heretics, with Stephen the general of piety commanding the ranks. For just as when Moses prayed Joshua routed the enemies, so also I, with the martyr working together with me, subdue the enemies of the truth. These things I say not trusting in abundance of words, but having confidence in the prayer of the martyr; therefore also with confidence I lay hold of the words. For I do not fear the bulk of their words. I am unafraid of the outworks of their evil-crafted deception. For I learned not to fear a fear where there was no fear. For they say that Christ fears and is afraid of death, but we for Christ's sake, as many days as we live in the flesh, so many times choose to die, in order that with bare head we may triumph over the truth. Therefore as already having the winning vote I advance against them. For Christ encourages me through the prophet saying: Son of man, do not be afraid of their face, because they will rage against you round about. For in the midst of scorpions you dwell. For I do not fear scorpions that sting. For I do not walk with bare foot; for I have the sandals of the gospel of peace, in order that even if I am bitten I may not be harmed. And having shod, he says, your feet in readiness of the gospel of peace. Come then, with the sandals of peace let us trample the many-formed head of the heretics, in order that through the things by which we fearlessly advance against them, we may teach them how greatly they err attaching fear and timidity to the nature of the only-begotten. For those who think and speak all things without judgment and without reason and do not understand the 'Father if possible let this cup pass' vote fear against Christ and say that he is needy and lesser because he prays to the Father and seeks release from the pressing necessity. Since therefore for insult of God they slander the Word of God and for rejection of the spirit they chant around the letter, mocking and ridiculing the plan of salvation of Christ, and with cleverness of phrase and fluency of words they cover over their venomous bites, robbing the more innocent of salvation, come, as those inexperienced in words let us call upon the very Word of God, in order that he himself becoming interpreter of his own words may expose the folly of those men, and may strengthen our understanding. Tell us the meaning of the things said, Master, unfold the leaf of the letter and show the fruit of the spirit, in order that we may not attend to the letter and die, but in order that running to the spirit we may enjoy life. For the letter kills, but the spirit gives life. Teach us as an infant, but discipline the heretics as fools; for you are the corrector of fools and teacher of infants. To us as infants bare the breast of grace and give the nipple of the spirit. Let the pure milk of the gospel teaching be poured out. But make the folly of the heretics clear. For if they were not fools, they would not have woven a doctrine of blasphemy for the destruction of your divinity. For the fool said in his heart, he says, there is no God. Bare their pretext of impiety, in order that the drama of hypocrisy may appear. Show that for this reason they carry around your name, in order that they may cover over the blasphemy of their own choice. Say then, Master, for what reason having come to the passion you decline to suffer, and why do you fear the threat of the Jews, you who command not to fear those who kill the body. And altogether if you fear death, why do you not decline death? For if in you lies the suffering and the not suffering, you say superfluously the 'If possible let it pass.' For in you

choices.why: Military metaphor: the heretics' deception is a fortified position with defensive projections; 'outworks' preserves the siege imagery.

choices.english: we may triumph over the truth
choices.why: The verb takes the truth as direct object; the sense is displaying the truth in triumph, not being triumphed over by it.
rejected: we may lead the truth in triumph

choices.why: The verb means to sing around or encircle with song; it conveys the heretics' ritualized, repetitive misuse of the letter.
The verb is judicial: to cast a vote against someone. The heretics pass a verdict of fear upon Christ.
The verb means to strip or plunder; the heretics despoil the innocent of their salvation.
The diminutive of φύλλον, a leaf or page; the image is of unfolding a written page to reveal the spiritual fruit.

pass_b_english: Again, as a soldier under orders, I take up the battle against the heretics, with Stephen, the general of piety, commanding the ranks. For just as Joshua routed the enemy while Moses prayed, so I too, with the martyr as my ally, subdue the enemies of the truth. I say this not because I trust in an abundance of words, but because I have confidence in the martyr's prayer; and so it is with confidence that I lay hold of these words. For I do not fear their bombast in speech. I do not fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception. I have learned not to fear a fear where there was no fear. They say that Christ fears death and is afraid of it, but we, for Christ's sake, choose to die as many times as the days we live in the flesh, so that with bare head we may lead the truth in triumph. Therefore, as one who already holds the winning vote, I advance against them. For Christ encourages me through the prophet, saying: "Son of man, do not be afraid of their faces, for they will rage against you on every side. For you dwell in the midst of scorpions" (Ezekiel 2:6). I am not afraid of stinging scorpions. For I do not walk with bare feet; I have the sandals of the gospel of peace, so that even if I am bitten, I am not harmed. "And having shod your feet," he says, "with the readiness of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15). Come then, with the sandals of peace let us trample the many-formed head of the heretics, so that by the fearlessness with which we advance against them, we may teach them how greatly they err when they attach fear and timidity to the nature of the only-begotten. For those who think and speak everything without judgment and without reason, and who do not understand "Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass," vote fear against Christ and say that he is needy and lesser because he prays to the Father and seeks release from the necessity pressing upon him. Since, then, they slander the Word of God to insult God, and to reject the Spirit they chant the letter around, mocking and ridiculing the plan of salvation of Christ, and with cleverness of phrase and fluency of words they cover over their venomous bites, robbing the more innocent of their salvation—come, as those unskilled in words, let us call upon the very Word of God, so that he himself, becoming the interpreter of his own words, may expose their folly and strengthen our understanding. Tell us the meaning of what has been said, Master; unfold the leaf of the letter and show the fruit of the Spirit, so that we may not attend to the letter and die, but may run to the Spirit and enjoy life. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). Teach us as infants, and discipline the heretics as fools; for you are the instructor of fools and the teacher of infants. To us as infants, bare the breast of grace and offer the nipple of the Spirit. Pour out the pure milk of the gospel teaching. And make the folly of the heretics plain. For if they were not fools, they would not have woven a doctrine of blasphemy to destroy your divinity. For the fool has said in his heart, it says, "There is no God" (Psalm 14:1). Strip bare their mask of impiety, so that the drama of their hypocrisy may be exposed. Show that they carry your name around for this reason: to cover over the blasphemy of their own choice. Tell us, then, Master, for what reason you came to the passion and yet decline to suffer, and why you fear the threat of the Jews—you who command us not to fear those who kill the body (Matthew 10:28). And if you fear death at all, why do you not decline death? For if it lies within your power to suffer or not to suffer, you say in vain, "If it is possible, let it pass." For in you—

problems.why: θριαμβεύω takes accusative of object triumphed over, not for; 'triumph in the truth' or 'lead truth in triumph'

problems.quote: I am unafraid of the outworks of their evil-crafted deception
problems.source_quote: Ἀφοβοῦμαι τῆς κακοτέχνου ἀπάτης τὰ προβλήματα
problems.why: Ἀφοβοῦμαι means 'I fear,' not 'I am unafraid'; the negation is wrong
problems.fix: I fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception
problems.ruling: Ἀφοβοῦμαι means 'I fear'; English 'unafraid' reverses the meaning. Must be fixed.

edits.old: so that with bare head we may triumph over the truth
edits.new: so that with bare head we may lead the truth in triumph

edits.old: I am unafraid of the outworks of their evil-crafted deception
edits.new: I fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception

fixed: Corrected 'triumph over the truth' to 'lead the truth in triumph' (θριαμβεύσωμεν τὴν ἀλήθειαν: accusative is the object led in triumph).
Corrected 'I am unafraid' to 'I fear' (Ἀφοβοῦμαι means 'I fear'; the negation was wrong).

problems.quote: I fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception
problems.source_quote: Ἀφοβοῦμαι τῆς κακοτέχνου ἀπάτης τὰ προβλήματα
problems.why: Source says 'I do not fear' (ἀφοβοῦμαι), not 'I fear'. Negation dropped, flipping the meaning.
problems.fix: I do not fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception.
problems.ruling: Ἀφοβοῦμαι = 'I am not afraid'; translator read as φοβοῦμαι, flipping meaning.

problems.source_quote: Εἶπεν γὰρ ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἄφρων, φησίν, οὐκ ἔστι θεός.
problems.why: The Greek quotes 'The fool has said in his heart, There is no God'—this matches Psalm 14:1 LXX (14:1/53:1). In LXX this is Psalm 13:1 or 14:1? LXX Psalm 13:1 = 'Εἶπεν ἄφρων ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ Οὐκ ἔστι θεός.' This is LXX Psalm 13:1, which is Hebrew Psalm 14:1. The English gives Psalm 53:1, which is the second occurrence. The source likely intends Psalm 14:1 (LXX 13:1) based on exact wording. Actually LXX 53:1 = Hebrew 53:1 is 'Εἶπεν ἄφρων...' too. But standard citation for this verse in Christian tradition is Psalm 14:1 (Hebrew) or 53:1. The LXX numbering is 13:1. The English uses Hebrew 53:1, but the more common citation is 14:1. However, 53:1 is also valid. Let me check if the work brief specifies: 'Psalms are cited according to the Septuagint numbering; modern citations should use corresponding Hebrew numbering where they differ.' LXX Psalm 13:1 = Hebrew 14:1. LXX Psalm 52:1 = Hebrew 53:1. The Greek here is likely LXX 13:1 (Hebrew 14:1), not Hebrew 53:1. The English 'Psalm 53:1' appears to be wrong—it should be Psalm 14:1.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 13:1 = Hebrew 14:1; English cites Psalm 53:1, a different psalm with same verse.

edits.old: I fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception.
edits.new: I do not fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception.

fixed: Source ἀφοβοῦμαι means 'I do not fear'; the English dropped the negation. Fixed to 'I do not fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception.'
The Greek quotation matches LXX Psalm 13:1, which corresponds to Hebrew Psalm 14:1, not Psalm 53:1. Fixed to Psalm 14:1.

problems.quote: to set aside the Spirit they chant around the letter
problems.source_quote: ἐπ' ἀθετήσει τοῦ πνεύματος τὸ γράμμα περιᾴδουσιν
problems.why: Greek means 'for the rejection of the Spirit they sing/chant the letter around', i.e., they use the letter to reject the Spirit; English reverses the relationship
problems.fix: to reject the Spirit they chant the letter around

edits.old: to set aside the Spirit they chant around the letter
edits.new: to reject the Spirit they chant the letter around

fixed: Changed 'to set aside the Spirit they chant around the letter' to 'to reject the Spirit they chant the letter around' to reflect the Greek 'ἐπ' ἀθετήσει τοῦ πνεύματος τὸ γράμμα περιᾴδουσιν' (for the rejection of the Spirit they chant the letter around).

dismissed.quote: to reject the Spirit they chant the letter around
dismissed.why: ἐπ' ἀθετήσει means 'for the rejection/setting aside of,' not 'to reject' as purpose; 'chant around' obscures mockery.
dismissed.note: ἐπ' ἀθετήσει with the dative states purpose, so 'to reject the Spirit' is right; 'chant around' is a fair rendering of περιᾴδουσιν and the complaint is about style.

dismissed.quote: they carry your name around for this reason: to cover over the blasphemy of their own choice
dismissed.why: προαιρέσεως = 'purpose/intention,' not 'choice' as faculty; 'cover over' weakens ἐπικαλύψωσιν.
dismissed.note: 'Choice' is a standard rendering of προαίρεσις and 'cover over' renders ἐπικαλύψωσιν accurately.

dismissed.quote: I do not fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception.
dismissed.why: Source says 'I am not afraid of' (ἀφοβοῦμαι), not 'I do not fear' — but the real issue: προβλήματα means 'pretexts/pretences', not 'outworks'.
dismissed.note: πρόβλημα can mean a barrier or defence put forward, which fits the soldier image here; 'I do not fear' and 'I am not afraid' say the same thing.

dismissed.quote: you who command us not to fear those who kill the body
dismissed.why: παρεγγυώμενος = 'you who pledged/promised' not 'command us'. The sense: Christ himself enjoined 'do not fear those who kill the body.'
dismissed.note: παρεγγυάω means to command or urge, and the reference is Christ's charge in Matthew 10:28, so 'command us' is correct and 'pledged' would be wrong.

dismissed.quote: Pour out the pure milk of the gospel teaching
dismissed.why: ἐπιχεθῇ = 'let it be poured out,' passive; subject is milk, not imperative to Christ.
dismissed.note: ἐπιχεθῇ is an aorist passive subjunctive (not optative) used as a request inside a prayer to Christ, so turning it into an imperative is a fair readable rendering.
